title: When the Sigil Burns Anew
premise: Theo Delacroix has spent ten years as the invisible keeper of the Thornfell gate, hiding a past he cannot remember and a sigil burned into his palm that aches whenever the wards are touched. When the wards collapse and the stars go dark, he learns he sold his own memories to the court beneath the mountain to seal it—and the price is coming due. To save the border, he must descend and steal back his soul, guided by smuggler Wren Ashvale, whose loyalty is tested when Theo's recovered memories reveal Wren's family helped make the bargain. In the end, Theo must choose between restoring what he was and becoming what the gate needs: he burns the sigil anew, binding himself as the living ward, and Wren chooses to stand watch beside him.
about_author: Orsen Nystrom is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. His work is known for quiet protagonists, haunted landscapes, and bargains that always cost more than promised.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Routine
chapters.summary: Theo inspects the Thornfell gate wards on an ordinary night, trading wry words with smuggler Wren Ashvale at the border tavern. His palm-sigil aches for the first time in years. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: comfortable invisibility about to shatter.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Every star over Thornfell goes dark at once, and the gate wards die with a sound like breaking glass. Theo's sigil flares white-hot, branding a word into his skin he cannot read. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror and the loss of his carefully hidden life.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Theo rides to the garrison town of Lowmark, where the magistrate reveals the wards weren't built to keep smugglers out but to keep something beneath the mountain sealed. She recognizes his sigil and calls it a 'debtor's mark.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dawning dread.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Wren offers to guide Theo through the mountain's back roads—routes only smugglers know—but demands to know the truth of his past first. Theo realizes he has no memories older than ten years. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: shame, and the first fragile trust.

chapters.title: Roads That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: They descend into the Thornfell passes, where the darkness has begun leaking upward: trees grow rings of black, and travelers wander memory-blind. Wren's knowledge keeps them alive. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: growing respect for the man she's guiding.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: They find a village whose inhabitants have forgotten their own names, living by rote. An old woman grabs Theo's hand, sees the sigil, and weeps, calling him 'the one who sold himself.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: horror that his bargain harmed others.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Deep Court
chapters.summary: In the village chapel, Theo finds a smuggler's ledger describing the court beneath the mountain: a goblin court that trades in souls and memory, ruled by the Broker. His own name appears in a ten-year-old entry. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the past becomes a map he must follow.

chapters.title: Ashvale's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Wren admits her family's smuggling routes were originally supply lines for the Broker's court—her grandfather helped deliver whatever Theo traded. Her loyalty wavers between family debt and the man beside her. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt and the choice to keep going anyway.

chapters.title: The First Toll
chapters.summary: At a mountain shrine, a toll-warden demands payment in memory. Theo pays willingly, losing the memory of his mother's face, and the warden's eyes widen: the court has marked him as overdue. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and urgency sharpening into panic.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Dark
chapters.summary: The Broker sends soul-hunters—hollow riders wearing the faces of the forgotten. A night chase through the passes ends with Wren wounded and Theo's sigil burning bright enough to drive them off. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Healer's Question
chapters.summary: A hermit healer tends Wren and asks Theo the question that guts him: if he recovers his soul, will he still be the man Wren trusts, or someone else entirely? Theo has no answer. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: identity crisis at the story's midpoint.

chapters.title: The Gate Below
chapters.summary: They reach the true gate beneath the mountain: the surface wards were only its echo. It stands open, and through it Theo glimpses the deep court—a city of candlelight and ledgers built from stolen years. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion.

chapters.title: Parley with the Broker
chapters.summary: The Broker, a courteous figure with Theo's forgotten face, offers a trade: his memories back in exchange for Wren's soul as payment of interest. Theo refuses; the Broker smiles, having expected it. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: temptation and defiance.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: While Wren distracts the court's clerks, Theo infiltrates the ledger room and finds his own contract—signed in his blood, witnessed by a name that makes him recoil: the Lowmark magistrate. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal discovered.

chapters.title: What Theo Bought
chapters.summary: Reading the contract, Theo recovers fragments: ten years ago he was the Broker's own clerk, who stole the master ledger of souls to seal the gate and erased his memory as payment. He wasn't a victim; he was a thief of hope. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: devastating self-knowledge.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Captured, Wren is offered her family's debt erased if she betrays Theo. She burns the Ashvale ledger instead, severing her family from the court forever, and breaks them both out. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over blood and safety.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Candle City
chapters.summary: A desperate escape across the deep court as the Broker unleashes every forgotten soul as hunters. Theo's sigil becomes a beacon, drawing the lost to follow him toward the gate. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: from fugitive to reluctant leader.

chapters.title: The Master Ledger
chapters.summary: At the gate, the Broker corners them and reveals the trap: Theo's theft left the ledger unbalanced, and the stars went out because the court is owed a soul of equal weight. Someone must stay. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the true cost made plain.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reforged
chapters.summary: Theo offers a new contract: not his soul, but himself—the sigil reborn as a living ward, his memories the ink. Wren witnesses it, refusing to let him sign alone, adding her name as guarantor. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into partnership.

chapters.title: When the Sigil Burns Anew
chapters.summary: The signing: fire, memory, and the Broker's ledger rebalanced as Theo becomes the gate's living seal. The stars return one by one. The Broker, bound by his own rules, withdraws beneath the mountain. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: climax—burning, transcendent loss.

chapters.title: What Remains of Theo Delacroix
chapters.summary: Theo wakes at the surface gate with fragmented memories—Wren's face he knows, his old life he doesn't. He is no longer who he was, but the sigil glows steady, and the border holds. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Keepers, Two
chapters.summary: Spring returns to Thornfell. Wren builds a cottage beside the gate, and together they keep the watch, teaching the forgotten village its names again. The sigil aches sometimes—but never alone. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution.
